name: canonify-objects-actions
description: The reference for Canonify's catalog mechanics: tables and auto-CRUD, bulk import, ObjectTypes (properties, enums, display, visibility, temporal), links and compound objects, ActionTypes (input, governance, idempotency, presentation), the handler DSL, state machines, schedules, and the built-in e-signature and outbox actions. Every JSON example decodes against the live validators. Read after the base `canonify` skill.

resources.title: Tables, auto-CRUD and import
resources.description: schema.propose_migration and its column conventions, what auto-CRUD generates (compound roots included), generated-update semantics, retyping a column, and bulk loading with objects.import.

resources.title: ObjectTypes — catalog.refine_object_type
resources.description: Every refinement field: mapped and derived properties, the ten property types, the JSON/boolean wire contract, enum narrowing, the valueColors token table, valueLabels, currency, labels, display (titles, forms, lists, action overrides), hidden and confidential, temporal effective dating, and re-refine hashes.

resources.title: Links, cardinality, compound objects
resources.description: Typed links (target, via, fk_on, cardinality), the on_delete policy honoured by every delete path, and compound objects: part_of rules, rollups, parts_frozen_when.

resources.title: ActionTypes — actions.declare
resources.description: Every declaration field: the input-type table, subject, governance and operation, unattended authority for schedules and reactions, the external-write target, idempotency postures and their windows, the transition marker, presentation, and actions.update.

resources.title: The handler DSL
resources.description: Refs, the eleven step kinds, the lead.convert example, predicates and where operators, nullable bindings, value expressions and dates, aggregates, set fan-out, fragments, on_fail, and every type-check error.

resources.title: State machines — state_machines.register
resources.description: Declaring a machine over an enum property, what a transition marker buys (guard, state write, hooks), moving a set in one call, why the bound property belongs to the machine, cross-validation and re-register hashes.

resources.title: Access — roles, groups and policies
resources.description: The member default, groups (groups/<name>.json in the bundle; add_member is user-only), the policies/<name>.json shape, row filters incl. :principal.groups and the via_link / exists link-through forms, governance.operation as a group gate, invokable: false and nav omission, and a runnable expense-claims example.

resources.title: Schedules & org lifecycle
resources.description: Declaring and operating schedules and reactions (schedules.declare, list, describe, history, run) and the org.* lifecycle actions (update, export, restore, delete, leave).

resources.title: E-signature actions
resources.description: The built-in e-signature actions you invoke: signature_request, signature, signature_envelope and member_signature — inputs, statuses, link_token redaction, consent and server-derived evidence, and the terminal lifecycle.

resources.title: Outbox actions
resources.description: outbox.inspect (queue health and rows, payload never returned, last_error redacted) and outbox.requeue (retry a deadletter or reclaim an abandoned claim), with their refusals. Requires manage authority.
